method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse paraphrase of every prose block, and exact formula, macro, token, identifier and conditional-file-ID comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Tableaux rules-and-proofs introduction: the signed-formula definition, intuitive sign readings, rule application along a branch, branch closure and the semantic force of a closed tableau rooted at a false-signed sentence.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section is Rules and Tableaux. A tableau systematically surveys ways a sentence may be true or false in a structure, using truth-value-signed formulas arranged in a downward-growing tree.
samples.checks: The section token remains exact. चिन्हांकित सूत्र and सत्यतामूल्याचे चिन्ह follow the standing signed-formula decision, while the source controls the semantic sense of possible truth and falsity in a structure.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A signed formula is a truth-value/sentence pair, either true-signed A or false-signed A. Informally these say that A might be true or might be false in some structure.
samples.checks: Both displayed signed formulas, their order and their truth signs are exact. The English word inside the display was translated to किंवा without changing the mathematical alternatives.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every tree entry is an assumption at the top or follows by an inference rule from an earlier signed formula. Each main operator has true- and false-sign rules; rules may branch or merely extend a branch and may need to use any earlier entry from the root to the application point.
samples.checks: The Marathi explicitly says that application is not restricted to the immediately preceding entry, so it preserves the source's any-earlier-entry permission rather than excluding the immediately preceding entry.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A branch closes when it contains both true-signed A and false-signed A; a tableau closes when every branch closes. Closure eliminates the described joint possibilities. A closed tableau for A has false-signed A at its root, so its existence eliminates every way A could be false and entails truth of A in every structure.
samples.checks: The same A occurs under both signs, the all-branches condition is retained, and the final direction runs from a false-signed root to truth in every structure. No validity or truth terminology is interchanged.
